title: Water Solubility at Saturation for CO2-CH4 Mixtures at 323.2 K and 9.000 MPa
experimental_method: in situ high-pressure infrared (transmission, 40 mm path) spectroscopic titration: calibrated 0.848 uL tubing loop meters water into the cell until the dissolved-H2O absorbance saturates; replicate titrations averaged
uncertainties_stated: u(T) = 0.1 K, u(P) = 0.005 MPa; u(x_Gr_CO2) = 0.03, u(x_GC_CO2) = 0.2 (mole percent); u(C_H2O) and u(x_H2O) expanded with coverage factor k = 10 (10 x standard deviation of replicates)
quality_remarks: The capture holds Table 1 as two records (and a third copy in the wrapper text) with different header whitespace; the cells are identical. Assembled once. Only one table exists in the paper (no Table 2).
Abstract: six CO2-CH4 mixtures at 323.2 K and 9.000 MPa: matches Table 1 (six rows).
Footnote e calls the uncertainties 'expanded ... coverage factor k = 10'; methods text says the error is conservatively estimated as 10 times the standard deviation; k = 10 is as printed.

Gas composition is the initially dry mixture (footnote b); measured water content is in the CO2-CH4 fluid at saturation with liquid water. Up to 1 % N2 + O2 (air) was detected by GC in some samples (footnote c).
rho in Table 1 is calculated with STOMP-COMP (footnote d), not measured; the x_H2O (permil) column is the authors' conversion of C_H2O, with their calculated densities.
Pure CH4 and CO2 rows: the abstract/text give 0.00 and 100.00 % as vendor-gravimetric; 'na' for GC.
Temperature scale and whether P includes water vapour are not stated; volume basis of C_H2O not stated.
